dataset.how_labelled: by construction: operators in flakeguard/injector insert each fault into a passing published test suite (cachetools); untouched tests are stable by observation (pristine suite passed in every pristine run)

tolerances.diagnosis: temperature 0 and a fixed seed: the same machine and Ollama version should repeat each reply; a repeat check of the none setting is stored
tolerances.tokens_and_chars: exact for the same code and prompt text

provenance.natural_flakes: none available: shown as a dash on the Results screen
limitations: No natural flakes (flakes found in real projects) were available. Natural results are not reported and stay dashes.

The injection operators produce the same fault classes the detector looks for (order, shared state, timing, randomness, clock), so injected results are only partly independent of the methods being evaluated.

B1 (fixed order) cannot see a fault that only an unusual order triggers, and the order-dependence pairs are built so that the setup test comes first in the default order (as a real order dependence usually does, or it would be found at once).

The time_tz faults fail only when the local hour is outside 8 to 17. Runs were made in the daytime, so those faults cannot fail in these runs by construction. The sensitivity table removes them; the primary table keeps them as flaky.

Tests no operator touched are labelled stable because the untouched suite passed in every one of its recorded runs. That is evidence, not proof; a rare flake in the library's own tests would be counted as a wrong flag.
26 flaky and 5 real tests among 476: small N for the flaky class. Intervals are wide.
B3's code features (the words sleep, random, datetime in the test source) read the text the operators insert, so B3 with them is partly circular; the run-features-only variant is reported next to it.
Identifiers chosen by the injection operators (for example _FLAKEGUARD_ORDER_READY, _race_flag) stay in the code the model sees, so the code settings are easier than real code.
One model (3B parameters, 4-bit), one prompt, one decoding setting. A different prompt could move every number.
26 injected flaky tests: a difference of a few tests between settings is inside the intervals.
Fix metric: N=5. No figure there is a rate.
provenance.what_the_model_sees: test id, run summary, and per setting the code described in docs/EVAL.md. Failure messages are never shown. Comment lines inserted by the injection operators and the message part of their asserts are removed (injected only).

sensitivity_if_random_were_accepted_as_r.note: NOT the result. The model sometimes wrote 'random' instead of the listed word 'randomness'. The registered rule counts that as a failure and the figure above does. This is what the count would be if it were accepted.
